thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — started seeing >200ms avg write latency on local NVMe across ~6 nodes in eu-west3, correlating with failed GPU allocations (pods stuck Pending).
ashley: which nodes? any SMART/metrics yet?
sanjay: node ids: gnode-ec2-1123, gnode-ec2-1147, gnode-ec2-1199. iostat snapshot:
```
Device:       tps  kB_read/s  kB_wrtn/s  await
nvme0n1      420   1024.00   12400.00    210.5
```
Also seeing lots of `io_context` stall logs in dmesg.
ops-bot: Alert: ephemeral-nvme-latency-spike detected on eu-west3 (6 nodes). Autocreated incident INC-2026-122.
kai: can you reproduce with fio quick-run? need to know if it's pathological writes or general queue depth.
sanjay: running quick fio now:
```
fio --name=seq-write --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --direct=1 --rw=write --bs=256k --numjobs=8 --iodepth=64 --size=1G --runtime=60
```
Result: sustained 45MB/s, 350ms lat tail.
ashley: yikes. sounds like firmware-level thermal or a GC/G room issue. Any recent scrub/cleaner overlap jobs? janitor runs in eu-west3 at 02:30 UTC.
devon: noticed a spike in overlayfs fsyncs from batch-worker pods earlier; GPU provisioning backlog increased ~12x in last hour. This will hit committed Dedicated capacity if not mitigated — cost and SLA risk.
kai: mitigation proposal — immediate: annotate nodes as `local-nvme=quarantine`, cordon + drain non-critical pods, and put them into a maintenance pool so the scheduler won't place new GPU workloads. This buys time and reduces provisioning failures.
ashley: agree. also throttle janitor scrub on eu-west3 and lower `scrub_parallelism` to 1 for the cluster. ops-bot, can we patch the cron remotely?
ops-bot: Command queued: `PATCH /infra/cronjobs/janitor` — set SCRUB_PARALLELISM=1 for eu-west3. Will apply in 90s.
sanjay: applying cordon/annotate now:
```
kubectl annotate node gnode-ec2-1123 infra/local-nvme=quarantine --overwrite
kubectl cordon gnode-ec2-1123
kubectl drain gnode-ec2-1123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```
oncall: please do `kubectl drain` only for safe pods — we shouldn't mass-evict GPU training jobs. use `--pod-selector` to prefer stateless.
kai: while nodes are quarantined, run `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` and `nvme-cli error-log` and capture firmware counters. If firmware GC/thermal counters spike, escalate to vendor RMA/firmware rollback.
ashley: I grabbed smart snippet from gnode-ec2-1123:
```
SMART Health Status: WARNING
Temperature: 85 C
Media Errors: 32

Firmware: 3.14.7
```
devon: temp 85C — that's a thermal/throttling situation. Possible datacenter cooling anomaly or drive failing under write amplification. Let's shift scheduled large batch jobs away from eu-west3 to us-west1 until cleared.
sanjay: migrating queued jobs now via scheduler label `region:prefer=us-west1` for the next 3 hours.
ops-bot: Scheduler override applied for batches with tag `bulk-training` — routing to us-west1.
kai: short-term software mitigations: reduce default iodepth for our GPU inference images to 32, enable read-only mounts for model caches on quarantined nodes, and reduce kv-cache persistence to avoid large writes.
ashley: long-term: open ticket with NVMe vendor (SN: XYZ-1123) for RMA and request firmware downgrade to 3.14.5 (last-known-good). Also add node-level thermal metrics to node exporter alert thresholds.
devon: cost note — moving jobs increases egress and inter-region cost; but cheaper than SLA penalties and reserved commit exposure. I'll draft a short tradeoff note for finance — estimated incremental cost ~ $1.2k/day while eu-west3 under mitigation.
oncall: action items:
 - ashley: throttle janitor + collect nvme logs + file vendor ticket (ETA 2h)
 - sanjay: cordon/quarantine nodes + run fio/smart + collect dmesg (ETA 30m)
 - kai: prepare scheduler routing override + small iodepth patch for images (ETA 1h)
 - devon: cost impact note and notify customers with reserved capacity (ETA 2h)

ashley: acked. starting vendor ticket now. putting a pinned message in the incident channel.
sanjay: initial drain complete for 3/6 nodes; two nodes showed immediate temp drop after cordon (fan ramp), but nvme error-log persistent.
kai: re-checking provisioning metrics — GPU pending count down from 120 -> 18 after routing override. Good.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-122 updated: nodes quarantined, janitor throttled, vendor ticket opened.
ashley: if any node becomes `ReadOnly` at block device level, don't reboot automatically — gather logs and vendor will request full nvme dump. Use `--no-reboot` in toolbox.
devon: will send the finance blurb in 30.
oncall: keeping this thread here for follow-ups. if we hit more than 10% capacity impact, escalate to Eng leadership. :raising_hand:
sanjay: will post a final status update in 2 hours or earlier if RMA/firmware action required. :thumbsup:
